evidence_summary: The authors described six bevacizumab-treated patients with renal lesions characteristic of thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). evidence_summary: Researchers disrupted ErbB2 specifically in ventricular cardiomyocytes using Cre-loxP in mice. The mutants developed severe dilated cardiomyopathy, usually showing cardiac dysfunction by their second postnatal month. This experimental result concerns genetically altered mice, not a treated patient cohort.
claim: This mouse experiment establishes the cardiomyopathy rate in patients receiving trastuzumab.

evidence_summary: Disrupting PD-1 in BALB/c mice caused dilated cardiomyopathy, impaired contraction and fatal heart failure. The phenotype did not occur in BALB/c mice also lacking RAG-2. Affected PD-1-deficient mice had circulating autoantibodies against a cardiomyocyte protein.
claim: PD-1 disruption caused cardiomyopathy in BALB/c mice even when RAG-2 was also absent.

evidence_summary: CTLA-4-deficient mice developed extensive lymphocyte proliferation and tissue injury, including severe myocarditis and pancreatitis. They died at three to four weeks of age. Their peripheral T cells were activated and could proliferate spontaneously.

evidence_summary: SOLAR-1 randomised 572 patients, including 341 with PIK3CA-mutated tumours. In the overall population, grade 3–4 hyperglycaemia occurred in 36.6% with alpelisib–fulvestrant versus 0.7% with placebo–fulvestrant. The abstract reported grade 3 diarrhoea, but no grade 4 diarrhoea.
claim: The reported 36.6% hyperglycaemia rate applies specifically to the PIK3CA-mutated subgroup.

evidence_summary: In CheckMate 067, treatment-related grade 3–4 adverse events occurred in 55.0% with nivolumab–ipilimumab, 16.3% with nivolumab alone, and 27.3% with ipilimumab alone. These are treatment-group event rates; they do not assign each event to a single molecular mechanism.
